reference.title: Files beside your tree
reference.shortdesc: The files you may see beside your tree: the tree itself and its backup.

section.p: When you open a family tree file, you may see more files beside it. makes the extra files for you. You do not need to open them or change them.

table.title: The files you may see beside your tree

row.entry: Your tree, such as Brontë family.ged
The file you opened. saves your changes to it.
The backup. Its name is the name of your tree, with the word backup, the date and the time added in brackets.
An older copy of your tree. makes one the first time it saves after you start the app.
No. It is an old version.

section.p: You may see more than one backup, because makes a new one each time you start the app and save. A backup is a family tree file too, so you can open one if you need your older tree.
A GEDZIP file, which ends in .gdz, holds the whole workspace in one file. It is the file to keep and to send. If you open a GEDZIP file, works on that file, and its backup is a GEDZIP file too.
Your tree may also link to pictures and other files. They are separate files, and a GEDZIP file holds them with the tree. says more.
To make the copy that you send, choose on the card for your tree. says more.
